context: Interactive hierarchical data table — a file system explorer with collapsible tree rows, sortable columns, live search, and two inline data encodings (spark bars + donut charts) per row.
first_impression: Clean, professionally composed table with deliberate typographic hierarchy and a thoughtfully chosen colorblind-safe palette, though the dual proportion columns feel redundant.
what_works: The Paul Tol palette is a genuinely intentional design choice — each top-level directory gets a distinct, harmonious hue that propagates through both spark bars and donuts, giving the eye an immediate visual anchor for tree membership. Typography is well-layered: uppercase tracked column headers, bold folder labels, lighter file labels, and monospace tabular numerics all create a readable hierarchy.
what_doesnt: The Proportion (spark bar) and Share (donut) columns encode the same quantity twice — this wastes column space and violates data-ink restraint without adding insight. The donut charts at 20×20 px are at the threshold of legibility, especially for small percentages where the arc segment nearly vanishes.
